title: What surprised you
hookLine: the thing you didn't expect to learn

cards: A boat pulls away from the shore with two travelers aboard. Once they're on board, one of them sets to work knocking a hole in its side. The other is Musa, a prophet, and he can't believe what he's seeing.
In Surat al-Kahf he set out on this journey to learn, and promised his teacher, a servant of Allah given knowledge from Allah's own presence, that he would be patient. He lasts until the boat.
You met this pair on day four hundred sixty-eight. Today, after a year of learning, the thing you didn't expect.

teach.h: A BOAT, A SECOND ACT, A WALL.
teach.b: In the Qur'an's telling, the boat is only the beginning. Musa protests. Then comes a second act, far harder, and Musa cries out against it.
Then, in a town that refused them food, the man rebuilds a falling wall for nothing, and Musa says he could at least have taken pay.
Each time the man reminds him, in paraphrase: did I not say you could not be patient with me? Then the explanations.
The boat belonged to poor people, and a king was seizing every boat by force; a damaged one would be passed by.
Under the wall lay a treasure belonging to two orphan boys whose father had been righteous, kept safe until they were grown.

teach.h: WHAT LOOKED WRONG WAS NOT YET KNOWN.
teach.b: What looked wrong was something Musa didn't yet know. Hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari name the man al-Khidr; the Qur'an simply calls him one of Allah's servants.
Musa was a prophet, and he still had more to learn, and the learning arrived as surprise.
The Qur'an elsewhere gives the Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, a line to say: "My Lord! Increase me in knowledge."
Surprise can be what that request looks like when it's answered. And your own year? Maybe it was that hadith scholars tested the words as well as the chain.
Or that, in Sahih al-Bukhari, Allah divided mercy into a hundred parts and sent down only one. Or that people of different schools stand in one row and no one corrects anyone.
Or something else entirely, that didn't go the way you expected.

how: Muslims read the story of Musa and al-Khidr in Surat al-Kahf, which some recite on Fridays, and teachers use it to speak about humility in learning and the limits of what a person can see.

o: the moment learning went somewhere you didn't expect
a fact so odd it must be a weak or made-up report
the part of the year you found too hard to follow

games.q: what surprised Musa — tap the pairs.

s: in the story, Musa already knew everything he needed
he set out to learn, and was surprised again and again.
the Qur'an itself names the man al-Khidr

their father had been righteous, and the treasure was kept until they were grown.

games.q: you're Musa. your teacher has just knocked a hole in the boat that carried you. you promised to be patient. what do you do?
games.why: Musa protests, and is reminded: did I not say you could not be patient with me? the explanation comes only at the end.

practice: Let the year go by slowly, like pages turning: the pillars, the reports, the schools, the creed, the heart, the manners, the life cycle, the world. Somewhere in there one thing may catch, a moment of wait, really?
Not the most impressive one, the one that actually caught: hold it for the rest of the sit, and find the one sentence that says it.

wordCard.voice: What surprised you. The moment a year of learning went somewhere you did not expect, which in Musa's story is where the learning really began. Today's word.

orig.note: Arabic: wonder, a marvel, the thing that makes you stop and stare.

carryVoice: Your line: surprised. In Musa's story, that's where the learning began. I'll be here tomorrow.
